sections: Abstract

We report mean annual runoff measurements from five monitoring stations collected between 2022 and 2024. A pilot survey in 2019 had put the regional mean annual runoff at 2791.5 mm; we find marked differences between upland and coastal sites.
1. Introduction
Earlier studies of sparse recovery relied on single-site records [1, 2]. A multi-site campaign makes it possible to separate local effects from regional trends [3].
2. Methods

Station metadata are listed in Table 1. Measurements follow the protocol of [3]. Values from the 2021 campaign are given in Table 3 for comparison and are not directly comparable with the 2024 campaign because the instruments changed.
3. Results
Table 2 reports the mean annual runoff for each station in the 2024 campaign. The largest change relative to 2021 was observed at station R-31.
4. Discussion
The spread between stations exceeds the measurement uncertainty, which suggests that site conditions dominate. Longer records are needed to confirm the trend.
References
[1] Nakamura et al. (2018). [2] Tanaka and Abernathy (2020). [3] Sørlie et al. (2021).
